notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Sources: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001628280-26-012254, filed February 26, 2026) and 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001628280-26-027203, ownership as of March 31, 2026). OWNERSHIP: the proxy gives Dorsey 1,000,000 Class A shares (marked *), 47,844,566 Class B shares (79.8% of Class B) and 42.2% of total voting power but no percentage of all shares, so pctEconomic is null and the 8.2% economic share is in leader.derived. He holds through two grantor retained annuity trusts, a trust in which he has a pecuniary interest, the Jack Dorsey Revocable Trust and Start Small, LLC. 5% HOLDERS: the proxy states Vanguard (12.8%), T. Rowe Price (8.8%) and BlackRock (7.3%) as % of Class A only; on an all-shares basis they would be lower (Class A is about 89.9% of all shares). They are recorded as stated, not recomputed. Their total-voting-power percentages are 6.0%, 4.2% and 3.4%. The Vanguard and BlackRock figures are as of September 30, 2025 and T. Rowe Price's as of June 30, 2025. The proxy adds that on March 26, 2026 The Vanguard Group filed a 13G/A saying that, after an internal realignment, certain subsidiaries and divisions will report beneficial ownership separately; the 12.8% is kept as the proxy's table states it. No dividends: Block has never paid any. Stock comp of $1,215.5 million is the cash-flow add-back. Geography: United States and International sum to total net revenue.

platformRevenue.label: Commerce enablement revenue (the revenue category that holds Square payments)

ecosystem.notes: measure is total GPV ($259.631B), which includes Cash App GPV. Square GPV alone is stated only rounded, as $250 billion, and is recorded in squareGPV, a schema extension. GPV excludes BNPL transactions. In FY2025 Block replaced its old revenue categories (transaction-based, subscription and services-based, hardware, bitcoin) with Commerce Enablement, Financial Solutions and Bitcoin Ecosystem, so transaction-based revenue is no longer reported. platformRevenue is therefore Commerce enablement revenue ($11.514B), the category that holds Square payment fees; it also includes software, hardware, Cash App Card, Cash App Pay, BNPL, Cash App Business and TIDAL revenue, so platformRevenue ÷ GPV overstates the take on payments alone and is not comparable with the FY2024 figure. Total net revenue was $24.194B, including $8.503B of bitcoin ecosystem revenue recorded gross. Revenue is reported in thousands and GPV in millions; both are converted to billions here.

taxes.notes: Taxes: the FY2025 income-tax note's table of income taxes paid by jurisdiction (federal 35,000; California 19,465; other state and local 31,869; United Kingdom 33,665; other foreign 9,391 thousand), total net of refunds; tagged us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaid. R&D not reported as a separate line. Block reports 'Product development' ($2,907,889 thousand in 2025; tagged us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense in XBRL), which the 10-K describes as engineering, data science and design personnel and infrastructure costs without calling it research and development, so it is not recorded.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001628280-26-012254). Payments company: formula with the sector flag. Revenue includes bitcoin ecosystem revenue of 8,502,787 thousand recorded gross, so the cost of the bitcoin sold counts in paidOut. Interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow; income taxes paid are from the income-tax note's table by jurisdiction (net of refunds). The held-for-sale loan flows inside OCF were a small net inflow in 2025, so the financeReceivablesInOCF bias is minor this year.

pay.notes: Employees: full-time head count at December 31, 2025, from the FY2025 10-K; temporary employees and consultants are not included. Payroll: the 10-K discloses no total staff cost, so the 2026 proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 is used (same year as the head count). The median excludes about 346 employees outside the U.S., Australia, Canada, Ireland and the U.K. After the year end, on February 26, 2026, Block announced a restructuring plan to reduce its workforce by more than 40% (FY2025 10-K, Note 22 Subsequent Events), so the year-end count overstates current staff.
